Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Who made the angels messengers having wings, two, three, or four. He increases in creation whatever He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾

Tafsir of Surah Fatir

It is Meccan.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: We have already explained the meaning of al-hamd (praise). His saying, ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, means: the One who brought them into being and created them without any precedent.

And His saying: ﴿Who made the angels messengers having wings﴾ means: possessors of wings.

And His saying: ﴿two, three, or four﴾ means: two-two, three-three, and four-four. Poetry on mathna (two-two):

(Ahmad Allah dhalika min liqa'... ahad ahad fi shahr halal)

Al-Dahhak said: "Mathna" is Jibril, "thula" is Mika'il, and "ruba" is Israfil. It is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I saw Jibril (peace be upon him) and he had six hundred wings, which filled the horizon." It is narrated that when he saw him in this form, he fainted. In some reports: "Jibril (peace be upon him) bathes every day in a river, then shakes himself off, and no drop falls except that Allah Most High creates from it an angel." Also, in some reports: Allah Most High created an angel in the heavens, honored him and raised him up, and in the report, [he has] of his greatness what Allah willed; he glorifies Allah Most High, and no utterance of his glorification falls except that Allah Most High creates from it an angel.

And His saying: ﴿He increases in creation whatever He wills﴾: The most apparent of the opinions is that Allah Most High increases in the creation of the angels and their wings whatever He wills, as we have mentioned. It is related from Qatadah who said: "He increases in creation whatever He wills" is good looks in life. It is related from al-Zuhri who said: it is beauty of voice. Al-Naqqash related in his tafsir that it is curly hair. It is related in some tafsirs that it is an increase in intellect and discernment. It is related from some that it is knowledge of crafts.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ means: capable.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 2:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whatever mercy Allah grants to people, none can withhold it﴾, i.e., of provision and rain. It was also said: of well-being. ﴿And whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him﴾, i.e., whatever He prevents, none can release it from after Allah, i.e., other than Allah.

It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say after the obligatory prayer: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things capable. O Allah, none can withhold what You have given, and none can give what You have withheld, and no status of a person of rank can benefit him against You."

It is also established that he said this phrase while standing between the bowing (ruku') and the prostration (sujud).

His saying: ﴿And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾, i.e., the Overpowering in His dominion (al-Jahim fi tadbir khalqih)...

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, remember the favour of God upon you﴾, meaning: the bounty of God upon you.

And His saying: ﴿Is there any creator other than God?﴾ is a rhetorical question (istifham) in the form of affirmation (taqrir), as if He had said: there is no creator other than God.

And His saying: ﴿who provides for you from the heaven and the earth﴾, meaning: from the heaven, the rain, and from the earth, the plants.

And His saying: ﴿There is no god but He; so how are you turned away?﴾, meaning: you are turned away from the truth.
And His saying: ﴿And if they deny you, then messengers before you were denied. And to Allah are returned all matters﴾, meaning: the matters are returned (to Him).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true﴾, meaning: the promise of the Resurrection is true.

And His saying: ﴿So let not the worldly life deceive you﴾. It is said in a report: Allah, may He be exalted, does not give anyone anything of the world except as a means of deception, and He does not withhold anything of the world from anyone except as a test.

And His saying: ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah﴾, meaning: let not the Deceiver deceive you, and he is Satan. Al-Hasan said: Among deception is that you commit disobedience and then wish for Allah's forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 6:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾ That is: oppose him by obeying Allah.

And His saying: ﴿He only invites his party﴾ That is: his followers.

And His saying: ﴿That they may be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ That is: that they may be in the Blaze (al-sa'ir), and al-sa'ir is the blazing fire.

Almost-complete translation:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who disbelieve, for them is a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾. That is: ʿaẓīm (great).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 8:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good...?﴾ The verse was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, ʿUtba, Shayba, al-ʿĀs ibn Wāʾil, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth, ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, and those like them. The second view is that the verse was revealed concerning the people of desires (ahl al-ahwāʾ) and innovations (ahl al-bidaʿ). The more preferable view is to say that the verse was revealed concerning the disbelievers, because most of the exegetes (ahl al-tafsīr) hold this view. It is reported from Qatada that he said: "Among them are the Khawarij, who consider the blood and property (of others) lawful." He said: "As for the people of major sins (ahl al-kabāʾir), they are not among them, because they do not consider major sins lawful." Likewise the unjust rulers (al-ʿummāl al-ẓalama), because they commit injustice while knowing that it is not lawful for them.

As for His words: ﴿so he sees it as good﴾ (and there is an ellipsis in the verse according to two methods). One of them: the meaning of the verse is, "Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good" like one whom Allah has guided? ﴿So indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.﴾ The second method: "Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so that he sees it as good" (is he like the one who is not?) Let not your soul go to waste in grief over them, for Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. Ḥasra (grief) is intense regret over what has passed.

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land﴾. That is: where nothing grows.

And His saying: ﴿So We revive thereby the earth after its death. Thus will be the resurrection﴾. That is: thus will be the resurrection in the Hereafter. Wakī' ibn ʿAdas narrated from Abū Razīn al-ʿUqaylī that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, how does Allah bring the dead to life?" He said to him: "Have you ever passed by a land that was barren, that is, dry, and then you passed by it when it was stirring green?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Thus does Allah bring the dead to life."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever desires honour﴾ — al-'Izzah (honour) is al-mana'ah (protection, inviolability).

And His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs all honour﴾. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of the verse is: whoever wishes to know to whom honour belongs, then to Allah belongs all honour. Qatadah said its meaning is: whoever desires honour, let him seek honour through obedience to Allah. The grammarians said: this is like when a person says, "Whoever desires wealth, then wealth belongs to so-and-so," meaning: let him seek wealth from so-and-so. Likewise, the meaning of His saying ﴿Whoever desires honour, then to Allah belongs all honour﴾ is: let him seek honour from Him. Some of the exegetes said: the people of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) worshipped idols and drew near to Allah through that, and sought honour from the idols. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah that they might be for them a source of honour﴾. So Allah sent down this verse and commanded them to seek honour from Allah, not from the idols.

And His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾. Regarding "the good word" there are several opinions. The first: it is "There is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illa Allah). The second: it is the Qur'an, related by Shahr ibn Hawshab. The third: it is the remembrance of Allah (dhikr). It is reported from Qatadah concerning ﴿The good word and righteous deed raise it, while those who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and their plotting will perish﴾: he said, "To Him ascends the good word," [meaning] Allah accepts the good word. It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "We do not narrate to you a hadith except that we bring you its confirmation from the Book of Allah, the Exalted." Then he said: "No servant says: Subhan Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu akbar, wa tabaraka Allah, except that an angel (malak) seizes them and gathers them under his wing, then ascends with them to the heaven. Then he does not pass by a company of angels except that they seek forgiveness for the one who said them, until he brings them before the Face of the Most Merciful." Then he recited His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it﴾. It was also said: the good word is the supplication (du'a') of the servants.

In some of the musnads, on the authority of Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "Allah, may He be exalted, says every day: I am the Mighty (al-'Aziz). Whoever desires the honour of both abodes, let him obey the Mighty."

And His saying: ﴿And the righteous deed raises it﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions. The first: what is related from al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and others, that they said: "And the righteous deed raises it" means the righteous deed raises the good word. The second opinion, the saying of Qatadah, who said: "And the righteous deed raises it" means Allah raises it.

The third opinion: "And the righteous deed raises it" means the good word raises the deed. The first of these sayings is the most preferable. It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: the word is presented to the deed; if it agrees with it, the word is raised together with the deed, and if it contradicts it, the deed is more deserving of being raised. In some reports: when a servant says "There is no god but Allah" with a sincere intention, it is raised to Allah, the Exalted, and it has a hum like the hum of bees, until it stands before Him, and Allah, the Exalted, looks at him with a look after which he will never despair. This is when his deed agrees with it; if his deed contradicts it, his word stops until he repents from his deed. (And if it contradicts it, it stops.)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who plot evil deeds﴾ — meaning: those who do evil deeds. It is said: it was revealed concerning the plotting of the disbelievers against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until he left Makkah as an emigrant to Madinah, as we have mentioned.

And His saying: ﴿For them is a severe punishment, and their plotting — it will perish﴾, meaning: it will be destroyed and invalidated.

The Qur'anic phrases in ﴿ ﴾ are given with their meaning.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 35, verse 11:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah created you from dust﴾. Al-turab (dust) is a finely ground body of the same kind as clay (tin).

And His saying: ﴿Then from a drop of semen﴾. Al-Suddi mentioned that when the drop of semen falls into the womb, it spreads into every bone, hair and sinew (asab). When forty days have passed, it descends into the womb, and Allah creates from it the clot (alaqah).

And His saying: ﴿Then He made you into pairs﴾, that is, kinds (asnaf). In the tafsir of Ibn Faris: ﴿He made you into pairs﴾ means a spouse for some of you from others.

And His saying: ﴿And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge﴾, that is, nothing of that escapes Him.

And His saying: ﴿And none is granted a long life, nor is his life shortened﴾, meaning: the lifespan of one who is granted a long life is not extended until he reaches old age. And His saying: ﴿nor is his life shortened﴾ refers back to the first. The answer: it is permissible for it to be mentioned in this way while meaning something other than the first, just as a man says: "I have a dirham and its half," meaning half of another dirham. This was cited by al-Zajjaj and others. The second view: ﴿And none is granted a long life, nor is his life shortened﴾ refers to the first (the same person). Ka'b al-Ahbar said when they [Umar] were present at Umar's death: "By Allah, if Umar asked his Lord to delay his term, He would delay it." They said to him: "Allah says: ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they hasten it﴾." He said: "That is when the term has arrived; but before that, it is permissible that it be increased and decreased," and he recited this verse. Some of them mentioned that an example of this is that Allah, the Exalted, writes that a person's life is one hundred years if he obeys Me, and his life is fifty or sixty if he disobeys Me, and this is permissible.

And His saying: ﴿except in a Book﴾, its meaning: except that it is written in a Book. In the tafsir it is said that Allah writes the servant's term in a Book, then writes in another Book: "A day, a month, a year has been subtracted from his life," until his term is fulfilled. Some of them mentioned that He writes it beneath that first Book.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, that is easy for Allah﴾, that is, easy.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the two seas are not alike: this one is sweet, fresh and pleasant to drink﴾, meaning: exceedingly sweet.

And His saying: ﴿pleasant to the drinker﴾, meaning: easy to enter (the throat).

And His saying: ﴿and this one is salty, bitter﴾, meaning: exceedingly salty. In the verse there is a demonstration of (God's) power in creating sweet and salty water.

And His saying: ﴿and from both you eat fresh flesh﴾, meaning: the fish.

And His saying: ﴿and you extract ornaments which you wear﴾: pearls, coral and jewels. ʿIkrima said: No drop falls from the sky to the earth except that it makes a herb grow, and no drop falls into the sea except that it becomes a pearl. If it is said: He has said, ﴿and you extract ornaments which you wear﴾, and pearls, coral and jewels are not extracted from the salty (sea) but only from the sweet (water)? And He has said, ﴿and from both you eat fresh flesh and you extract [ornaments]﴾. The answer to this: it is permissible to attribute it to both, even if it is extracted from only one of them, and the like of this is abundant in the speech of the Arabs.

The second answer: in the salty sea there are sweet springs, which mix with the salt, and among these (waters) jewels are formed.

And His saying: ﴿and you see the ships ploughing through it﴾. Al-Hasan said: "mawaqir", meaning: laden, full. It is reported from some of them: "mu'taridah" (crossing), coming and going. It was also said: "jawari" (sailing). The makhr is the cleaving, so it is as if the ship cleaves the water with its prow, and thus "mawakhir" is mentioned in this sense.

And His saying: ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾, meaning: that you may seek of His bounty, and His bounty is trade on the sea.

And His saying: ﴿and that you may be grateful﴾, meaning: that you may be thankful for the blessings of God.

قَوْله تَعَالَى: ﴿يولج اللَّيْل فِي النَّهَار﴾ قد بَينا هَذَا من قبل.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾ We have already explained this before.

وَقَوله: ﴿ [ويولج النَّهَار فِي اللَّيْل] وسخر الشَّمْس وَالْقَمَر﴾ قَالَ قَتَادَة: طول الشَّمْس ثَمَانُون فرسخا، وعرضها سِتُّونَ فرسخا. وَعَن عِكْرِمَة قَالَ: جرم الشَّمْس كسعة الدُّنْيَا (وَزِيَادَة ثلث، وجرم الْقَمَر كسعة الدني) بِلَا زِيَادَة.

His saying: ﴿[And He causes the day to enter into the night] and has subjected the sun and the moon﴾. Qatadah said: The length of the sun is eighty farsakhs (a unit of distance, about three miles), and its width is sixty farsakhs. It is reported from Ikrimah that he said: The body of the sun is the size of the world (al-dunya), (with an added third), and the body of the moon is the size of the world (al-dunya), without addition.

وَقَوله: ﴿كل يجْرِي لأجل مُسَمّى﴾ ظَاهر الْمَعْنى.

His saying: ﴿each runs for an appointed term﴾: its meaning is apparent.

وَقَوله: ﴿ذَلِكُم الله ربكُم لَهُ الْملك وَالَّذين تدعون من دونه﴾ أَي: من الْأَصْنَام.

His saying: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. And those you invoke besides Him﴾, i.e., the idols.

وَقَوله: ﴿مَا يملكُونَ من قمطير﴾ قَالَ مُجَاهِد: القطمير: لفافة النواة، وَهُوَ كسحل البصلة، وَعَن بَعضهم: القمطير وسط النواة، وَالْمعْنَى أَنه يملك شَيْئا قَلِيلا وَلَا كثيرا.

His saying: ﴿They do not possess even a qitmir﴾. Mujahid said: The qitmir is the thin membrane (lafafah) around the date-stone, and it is like the peel (sahl) of an onion. It is reported from some of them: the qitmir is the core (wasat) of the date-stone. The meaning is that they do not own anything, neither little nor much.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you call upon them, they will not hear your call﴾. He means: if you call upon the idols, they will not hear your call.

And His saying: ﴿And even if they heard, they would not respond to you﴾. That is: they would not answer you.

And His saying: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association (of them with Allah)﴾. That is: they will repudiate your polytheism and your allegiance to them.

And His saying: ﴿And none can inform you like one who is acquainted (with all things)﴾. That is: no one can inform you of this like me, and the Acquainted (al-Khabir) is Allah, exalted is He. The meaning is that the One who has informed you of this is All-Aware of affairs, knowing of them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 15:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah﴾, meaning: toward the bounty of Allah. And the faqir (poor one) is the one in need (muhtaj).

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy﴾, meaning: the One free of need from His creation, the One praised for His benevolence toward His creation.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away﴾, meaning: He can destroy you, until not a single eye of yours remains that blinks.

And His words: ﴿and bring a new creation﴾, meaning: a creation that they did not come into being from and that He did not originate and begin.
And His saying: ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾, meaning: not hard (shadid).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 18:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ means: no one is held to account for the sin of another.

His statement: ﴿And if one heavy-laden calls [another] to carry its load﴾ means: heavy-laden with sins, ﴿to [carry] its load﴾ means: if one calls upon someone to bear his sins for him.

His statement: ﴿not a thing of it will be carried, even if he were a near relative﴾ means: he will not find anyone to bear it for him, even if the one called upon is a close relative, a father or sons. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: On the Day of Resurrection a man will meet his father or his son, and say: "Bear some of my sins for me." He will say: "I cannot; my own burden is enough for me." In some tafsirs it is mentioned that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi said to those of Banu Makhzum who had embraced Islam: "Return from Islam, and I will bear your sins on the Day of Resurrection, if you fear sins." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

His statement: ﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾ — we have already explained the fear of the unseen (al-khashya bil-ghayb).

His statement: ﴿And establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself, he purifies himself only for his own benefit﴾ — the meaning of purification (tazakki) here is righteous action.

His statement: ﴿And to Allah is the destination﴾ means: the return.

Almighty God says: ﴿And the blind and the seeing are not alike﴾. The meaning of "the blind" is one who is blind to guidance, and "the seeing" is one who sees guidance. It is related from some of them: "the blind" is one blind to the truth, and "the seeing" is one who sees the truth.

And His saying: ﴿Nor are the darknesses and the light﴾. The "darknesses" are the misguidances, and "the light" is the guidance and clear proof from Allah, exalted is He. It has also been said: this is a parable for disbelief and faith.

And His saying: ﴿Nor is the shade and nor the scorching heat﴾, meaning: Paradise and the Fire. Abu Ubayda said: al-harur occurs during the day together with the sun. And from others: al-samum (the scorching wind) is by day, and al-harur is by night. And from some of them: al-harur is the constant heat, whether by night or by day. The poet said: (And a noontide heat whose scorching roasts the faces ...)

The Qur'an, 35:22, and its commentary by al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an):

And His saying: ﴿And the living and the dead are not alike﴾, meaning: the believers and the disbelievers. And it is related from Ibn Qutaybah that he said: the scholars and the ignorant.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills﴾, meaning: whom He wills to make hear.

And His saying: ﴿And you cannot make hear those who are in the graves﴾, meaning: you do not make the disbelievers hear, and He likens them to the dead in their graves.

Here is the translation:

And His saying: ﴿You are but a warner﴾, meaning: one who warns.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 24:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾, meaning: giving good tidings and giving warning.

And His saying: ﴿And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them﴾, meaning: a warner. In some tafsirs: "Except the Arabs, for they had no prophet other than the Prophet (ﷺ)."

In some narrations: Bahlul the madman met Abu Yusuf the judge, and said to him: "Indeed Allah the Most High says: ﴿And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them﴾, and the Prophet said: 'Were it not that dogs are a nation among the nations, I would have commanded their killing.' So what is the warner of the dogs?!" Abu Yusuf was perplexed; so he brought out a stone from his sleeve and said: "This is the warner of the dogs."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if they deny you, those before them had already denied; their messengers came to them with the clear proofs, and with the scriptures (zubur), and with the illuminating Book.﴾ That is, the clear Book. The mention of "the Book" after "the scriptures" is by way of emphasis.
The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then I seized those who disbelieved, so how was My rejection?﴾ That is: My denial and My changing (of their condition).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 27:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky﴾ (His words): ﴿and We bring forth thereby fruits of varying colours﴾, meaning: white, red, yellow, and the like.

And His words: ﴿And among the mountains are streaks (judad) white﴾, meaning: paths and stripes (and lines), ﴿white﴾. Al-judad is the plural of judda (jaddah), which is the path (ṭarīq).

And His words: (﴿and red﴾), meaning: paths of red.

His words: ﴿Of varying colours, and jet-black﴾, meaning: jet-black (sūd ghirābīb) with inversion of order (al-taqdīm wa'l-ta'khīr). It is said: aswad ghirbīb, meaning: intensely black. In some reports: "Indeed Allah dislikes the ghirbīb old man," meaning the one who blackens his beard. Dyeing with red is a sunnah, whereas dyeing with black is disliked (makrūh). The meaning of the verse is: black paths.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 28:

And His saying: ﴿And among mankind and the moving creatures and the cattle, [their] colours are likewise diverse.﴾ That is: the colours of these things differ, just as the colours of what was mentioned before differ.

And His saying: ﴿It is only those who have knowledge among His servants who fear Allah.﴾ Among what is well known in the reports (al-athar) is: "The head of knowledge is the fear of Allah." Also well known: "Fear of Allah is sufficient as knowledge, and self-delusion about it is ignorance." It is said: the first word in the Psalms (al-Zabur) is "The head of wisdom is the fear of Allah." And from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: ﴿It is only those who have knowledge among His servants who fear Allah﴾ means: those who know My kingship, My might and My dominion. And from some of them: ﴿It is only those who have knowledge among His servants who fear Allah﴾ refers to those who know that Allah is powerful over everything. And from some of the Successors (al-tabi'un) he said: "Whoever does not fear Allah is not a scholar." It is also said: Fear Allah according to the measure of His power over you, and be shy before Allah according to the measure of His nearness to you.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Mighty, Forgiving.﴾ That is: Mighty in His kingdom, Forgiving (of the sins of His servants).

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, hope for a commerce that will never perish.﴾ That is, it will never be destroyed and never be ruined. And what is meant by "commerce" is the reward that Allah has promised.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 30:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That He may give them their rewards﴾ means: the reward of their deeds.

And His saying: ﴿And increase them of His bounty﴾ is the multiplying of the good deeds. Some of them said: it is intercession (shafa'ah) for those who did good to them. Accordingly, the poor man intercedes for the rich man who gave charity to him.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾ it is said: He forgives much of the sins and appreciates little of the acts of obedience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 31:

The words of His, exalted is He: ﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what is before it⦆. That is: of the earlier scriptures.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.﴾ That is: Acquainted with what is in their inner selves, Seeing [of their deeds].

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 32:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾. Most scholars hold that what is meant by His saying ﴿those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾ is this community (ummah). It is reported from some of them that what is meant is the prophets, and from some of them that what is meant is the Children of Israel. The first view is the well-known one.

His saying ﴿We caused to inherit the Book﴾: what is meant by the Book is the Qur'an.

The meaning of the verse: that is, the matter has reached them through Our sending down the Qur'an to them and Our sending Muhammad (ﷺ) to them.

His saying ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾: scholars differ concerning what is meant by "the one who wrongs." Some said: what is meant by the wrongdoer is the disbeliever; this was related by al-Kalbi and others. It is also reported from some of them that what is meant is the hypocrite. On this view, the wrongdoer is not included in His saying ﴿gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾. This view has also been related from Ibn 'Abbas, who took "the wrongdoer" to mean the disbeliever.

The well-known view is that "the one who wrongs himself" is among the believers, and on this view the sequence of the verse is coherent. On the first view, His saying ﴿those whom We have chosen from among Our servants﴾ is understood as chosen-ness in creation, the sending of the Messenger, and the sending down of the Book. On the second view, the chosen-ness is understood as the excess which God, the Exalted, granted to this community above all other communities. Shahr ibn Hawshab reported that 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) said: "Our foremost is foremost, our moderate is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven." It is also reported from 'A'ishah (رضي الله عنها) that she said: "The foremost are those who passed away in the time of the Prophet, the moderate are those who followed them, and the wrongdoer is like me and like you," saying this to the one addressed.

It is reported from Abu al-Darda' that he said: "The foremost is the one who is not called to account at all on the Day of Resurrection; the moderate is the one who is called to account with an easy reckoning and enters Paradise; the wrongdoer is the one who is called to account with a severe reckoning, enters the Fire, and then is saved."

It is reported from some of them that the one who wrongs himself are the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'amah), the moderate are the companions of the right (ashab al-maymanah), and the foremost are those brought near (al-muqarrabun); this was related by al-Suddi. On this view, the one who wrongs himself is a disbeliever. It is reported from some of them that the one who wrongs himself are the companions of the major sins, the moderate are the companions of the minor sins, and the foremost is the one who has committed neither a minor nor a major sin. Some of them expressed this by saying: "The moderate are those who are balanced in acts of obedience." On this view, whoever's bad deeds outweigh his good deeds is a wrongdoer; whoever's bad and good deeds are equal is moderate; and whoever's good deeds outweigh his bad deeds is foremost. This is a known view, transmitted [from the Messenger of God].

It is reported from some of them that he said: "The wrongdoer is Adam, the moderate is Abraham, and the foremost is Muhammad." Some said: "The wrongdoer is the seeker (al-murid), the moderate is the lover (al-muhibb), and the foremost is the one utterly bewildered (al-walih)." Some said: "The wrongdoer is the one whose concern is himself and this world, the moderate is the one whose concern is Paradise, and the foremost is the one whose concern is his Lord."

It is reported from some of them that he said: "The wrongdoer is the one who stands still (al-waqif), the moderate is the one who travels (al-sa'ir), and the foremost is the one who has arrived (al-wasil)." There is much discussion concerning the verse.

His saying ﴿Among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds by God's permission﴾: that is, in acts of obedience, by God's knowledge.

His saying ﴿That is the great bounty﴾: that is, the great favour.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 33:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾. It is narrated from Ja'far al-Sadiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The most hopeful verse in the Book of Allah, Exalted is He, is this verse, because it gathers together the wrongdoer (zalim), the moderate (muqtasid) and the foremost (sabiq), and then says: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence which they will enter﴾." It is also narrated from some of them that he said: "The waw in His saying ﴿they will enter it﴾ is more beloved to me than such-and-such." And it is narrated from many of the early generations (al-salaf) that they said: "All of these are included in this verse."

His saying: ﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾ — its meaning is apparent. Al-asawir (bracelets) is the plural of siwar (bracelet).

His saying: ﴿and pearls﴾ — meaning: [adorned with] gold and pearls. It was also read as "wa-lu'lu'an" in the accusative, meaning: they will be adorned with pearls.

His saying: ﴿and their clothing therein is silk﴾ — meaning: brocade (dibaj). It is well known that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter," and he said: "It is for them in this world, and for us in the Hereafter."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us grief."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "The grief of the Fire." It is related from Qatadah: "The grief of death." It is related from some of them: "They are the livelihood."

Mujahid said: "They are the bread." The more appropriate view is that it be understood as encompassing all griefs, for they are saved from all of them. And it is well known that the grief is the grief of the terrors of the Resurrection.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, our Lord is All-Forgiving, All-Appreciative.﴾ It has already been explained.

The words of the Most High: ﴿Who has settled us in the abode of permanence, out of His bounty﴾. We have already explained the meaning of "al-maqama" and "al-maqama."

And the words of the Most High: ﴿No weariness touches us therein, nor does fatigue touch us therein﴾. That is, toil (taʿab) and exhaustion (iʿyaʾ).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve, for them is the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed upon them so that they die﴾. That is: death is not decreed upon them so that they would die.

And His saying: ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾. That is: from the punishment of the Fire.

And His saying: ﴿Thus do We recompense every ungrateful disbeliever﴾. That is: ungrateful for the blessing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 37:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will cry out therein﴾ — yaṣṭaraẖūna (يصطرخون) is of the form yaftaʻilūna (يفتعلون), derived from al-ṣurākh (الصُّرَاخ), which is shouting.

And His saying: ﴿"Our Lord, bring us out"﴾ — meaning: they will cry out and say, "Our Lord, bring us out, that we may do righteous deeds other than what we used to do." That is, that we may do righteous deeds instead of the evil deeds we used to do.

And His saying: ﴿"Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed?"﴾ — meaning: Allah, Exalted is He, will say to them, "Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would take heed to take heed?" Its meaning: Did We not give you the lifespan in which whoever would be mindful would be mindful? Scholars differed regarding that lifespan. The majority hold that it is sixty years, and this is related from ʿAlī (raḍiya Allāh ʿanhu). Abū Hurayrah has also related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever Allah grants a lifespan of sixty years has left him no excuse regarding his life." Others hold that it is forty years. Others hold that it is eighteen years. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: it is puberty (al-bulūgh). Others hold that it is seventy years, because at that point one enters old age (al-harm).

And His saying: ﴿And the warner came to you﴾ — meaning: Muḥammad (ﷺ).

The second view: it is gray hair (al-shayb). This is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih and others. In a report: "No hair turns white except that it says to its sister: 'O my sister, prepare yourself, for death has drawn near.'" Some said: gray hair is the debris (ḥuṭām) of death. And some called it the messenger (barīd) of death.

The third view: that His saying, ﴿And the warner came to you﴾, refers to everything that warns and frightens with it. In Gharīb al-Tafsīr it is said that it is fever (al-ḥummā). It has also been said that it is reason (al-ʿaql).

And His saying: ﴿So taste, for there is not for the wrongdoers any helper﴾ — meaning: any naṣīr (helper).
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾ (the verse). The meaning is apparent.

He, the One who made you successors (khala'if) upon the earth. That is: some of you succeed others. Everyone who follows a person and stands in his place after him is his successor (khalifah). For this reason Abu Bakr was called Khalifat Rasul Allah (the successor of the Messenger of Allah), because he took up the affair after him. Otherwise, according to the people of knowledge, the Messenger died and did not appoint anyone as successor. From this is the saying of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, when death approached him, and it was said to him: "Appoint a successor." He said: "If I do not appoint one, then the Messenger of Allah did not appoint one; and if I appoint one, then Abu Bakr appointed one." This is an established report from Umar.

And His saying: ﴿So whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾, that is: upon him is the burden (wabal) of his disbelief.

And His saying: ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them, in the sight of their Lord, except in hatred﴾, that is: in aversion (maqt), meaning hatred. It was also said: it is that which makes them deserving of aversion.

And His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss﴾, that is: in ruin (khusran).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 40:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah?﴾ That is: those whom you made My partners according to your claim, from among the idols and the angels.

And His saying: ﴿Show me what they have created of the earth﴾ That is: inform me.

And His saying: ﴿Or do they have a share (shirk) in the heavens?﴾ That is: a partnership (shirka).

And His saying: ﴿Or have We given them a Book so that they are upon clear evidence from it?﴾ That is: upon clear proofs from it.

And His saying: ﴿Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion﴾ That is: the wrongdoers do not promise one another anything but ghurur (delusion), and ghurur is everything that deceives a person, of what has no basis.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 41:

The words of God Most High: ﴿Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they should cease [to exist]﴾. Its meaning is: lest they should cease. It has also been said: out of aversion that they should cease.

And His words: ﴿And if they were to cease, none could hold them after Him﴾, meaning: no one other than Him holds them. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿And if they were to cease﴾, when they do not cease?

The answer: God Most High has said: ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son﴾. And God Most High holds them back from these things. In some reports it is related that Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, how can I know that You do not sleep?" So He placed two flasks in his hands, as we have mentioned.

In some tafsirs: the earth is heavy and sinking, and the sky is light and spreading out, and God Most High has joined the extremities of the heavens to the extremities of the earths. So the sky, by its rising, prevents the earth from sinking, and the earth, by its weight, prevents the sky from ascending. This was related by al-Naqqash. And God knows best.

His words: ﴿Indeed He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving﴾. If it is asked: what is the meaning of mentioning forbearance here?

We say: because these things were about to do what they were about to do as a punishment for the disbelievers, so God Most High held them back, and did not allow them to cease, refraining from hastening the punishment; and that was forbearance on His part, may His majesty be exalted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 42:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most solemn oaths﴾ refer to the polytheists of Mecca. They had said: "If a warner comes to us, we will be better guided (ahda) than any one of the nations," meaning: more ready to accept the Book (aqbal lil-kitab) and more committed to it (alzam lahu) than the Jews and the Christians. But when the Messenger came to them, they did not fulfill what they had said. So Allah the Exalted revealed concerning them ﴿If a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any one of the nations﴾, which is the meaning of His words, namely, the Jews and the Christians.

As for His words ﴿But when a warner came to them﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿it increased them in nothing but aversion﴾, meaning: his coming increased them in nothing but aversion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 43:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Arrogance in the land﴾, meaning: they rejected what they rejected out of arrogance in the land.

And His saying: ﴿and the evil planning﴾, meaning: and they committed the evil planning. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "wa-makran sayyi'an" (and an evil scheme). Regarding the evil planning there are two views: the first is that it is shirk (polytheism), and the second is that it is planning against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

And His saying: ﴿And the evil planning does not encompass anyone except its own people﴾, meaning: the punishment of the evil planning does not descend except upon its people, and the real meaning is that the harm of the planning returns to them.

And His saying: ﴿So do they await anything but the way of the earlier peoples?﴾ (meaning: the course of the earlier peoples) in destruction and the descent of punishment upon them.

And His saying: ﴿So you will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any alteration in the way of Allah﴾ — the meaning is apparent, and the purpose of the repetition is emphasis.

Almighty God's saying: ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them, though they were greater than them in strength? And God is not one to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on earth; indeed He is ever All-Knowing, All-Powerful.﴾ That is: "to escape Him" (layuft 'anhu), i.e., so as to get away from Him.

And His saying: ﴿anything in the heavens or on earth; indeed He is ever All-Knowing, All-Powerful.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 35, verse 45:

The Most High's saying: ﴿And if Allah were to take the people to task for what they have earned﴾ from abominations and sins.

And His saying: ﴿He would not leave upon it (the earth's back) a single creature﴾, meaning: upon the surface of the earth, because of what people have earned of sins. It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "Indeed, the dung beetle is punished in its hole for the sin of the son of Adam."

And His saying: ﴿But He defers them until a specified term﴾, meaning: until a known period.

And His saying: ﴿So when their term comes, then indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants﴾, meaning: Seeing of their deeds, recompensing them for them: good with good, and evil with evil.
